First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/2}^{e/2}-{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,(x){|}_{1/2}^{e/2}-{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{e}{2})\,(\frac{e}{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{1}{2})\,(\frac{1}{2})]-{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{e}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-x{|}_{1/2}^{e/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}e-\frac{1}{2}e+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
